idiom_name: host type parameterized on policy units with a documented contract
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: split the component's design decisions into named, orthogonal axes; give each axis a contract (the members a policy must provide) plus at least one default implementation; make the host parameterized on the policy units and route each axis through its policy at the points where the decision is consumed. Keep the binding at type/instantiation time so no call is indirect, and document the contract explicitly because most languages cannot express it. Where the language cannot parameterize by type, or the choice must be made after instantiation, stop at the boundary and expose a Strategy-style constructor parameter instead.
code_sketch:
host = make_host(StoragePolicy, OwnershipPolicy, CheckingPolicy)
host.store(value)          # -> StoragePolicy.store
host.release(value)        # -> OwnershipPolicy.release
# each axis is a named, separately documented contract with a default,
# so clients bind only the axes they actually vary
pitfalls: Leaving the policy contract undocumented: the host then depends on members nothing declares, and a policy change breaks callers silently.
Parameterizing axes that never vary: the host gains template complexity but no new combination is ever instantiated.
Trying to express runtime variation: policies bind when the host is instantiated, so a configuration-time choice needs a Strategy or type-erasure layer.
